info.title: tommy events API
info.description:
The events API: everything an application under test needs to read back what it
sent.

Tommy stands in for the services an application talks to - mail providers, SMS
gateways, file transfer, chat webhooks, EDI partners - and records every message
it receives as an event. These routes list those events, fetch one in full,
stream them as they arrive, delete them, and download the bytes any of them
carried. Every event names the page that renders it, so a test can print a link
to what it just sent.

Two things are deliberately absent. The fake vendor endpoints - Mailjet's send
API, Twilio's, Slack's - are those vendors' specifications rather than tommy's,
and a partial copy of somebody else's API is worse than none; run `tommy providers`
for those. And each plugin's own read-back routes (`/api/v1/mail/messages` and its
kin) are a convenience on top of these, shaped by the content type rather than
by a contract worth generating a client from; each plugin's README documents its
own.

This document is generated from the server's route table. It cannot describe a
route that does not exist, and CI fails if the checked-in copy stops matching
the code.

get.summary: The bytes an event carried - a mail attachment, an uploaded file - streamed with range support. Events reference these by the id in their payload rather than inlining them.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The event id, as returned by any listing.

parameters.name: inline
parameters.description: Serve with an inline Content-Disposition rather than as a download.

400.description: A query parameter could not be parsed - a malformed since, a negative limit.

404.description: No such resource, or it belongs to another plugin.

get.summary: Every captured event, newest first, whatever plugin captured it. Raw request bodies are omitted unless asked for: they can be megabytes each.

parameters.name: plugin
parameters.description: Only events from this plugin, such as mail.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Only events captured by this provider, such as mailjet.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only events of this type, such as mail.message.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring over the summary and type.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: RFC3339 timestamp, a duration such as 5m, or unix milliseconds.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many events to skip.

parameters.name: include_raw
parameters.description: Include each event's raw request body.

400.description: A query parameter could not be parsed - a malformed since, a negative limit.

delete.summary: Clear captured events, all of them or one plugin's. Stored payloads deliberately survive, so a link to one already handed out keeps working.

parameters.name: plugin
parameters.description: Clear only this plugin's events.

400.description: A query parameter could not be parsed - a malformed since, a negative limit.

get.summary: The same events as they arrive, as Server-Sent Events. Each event produces a JSON frame carrying the event without its raw body, and a frame named after the event type carrying just the id, so an htmx page can trigger on it.

parameters.name: plugin
parameters.description: Only events from this plugin, such as mail.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Only events captured by this provider, such as mailjet.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only events of this type, such as mail.message.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring over the summary and type.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: RFC3339 timestamp, a duration such as 5m, or unix milliseconds.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many events to skip.

400.description: A query parameter could not be parsed - a malformed since, a negative limit.
